## 6. WRITE ROUTES

### Composed route, primary

Flow Mode composes the board itself. `scripts/compose_board.py` reads the checked model and fills `assets/compose-board.js`, and one `use_figma` call runs that code in the file the gate named. The call draws a framed board: the title and the subtitle, the diagram with its zones, every shape sized to its text and coloured by its kind, the routed connectors, a key of every mark the board uses and the source line, all on an 8 pixel grid. It draws every type in Section 3.

The route is a native MCP connection to Figma's server at `https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`, which Figma's own plugin declares in its root `mcp.json`. The connection comes from that plugin or from the client's connector. Code Mode holds no manual for Figma's hosted server here, and its `figma` manual runs Framelink's `figma-developer-mcp` instead. Whether Figma's OAuth-gated server would admit a Code Mode client is unverified. The vendored `mcp-figma` packet's wiring guide covers that Code Mode path, and its Section 6 records how a headless Claude Code or Codex child reaches the hosted server. The `allowed-tools` frontmatter of this packet names Code Mode as its only MCP tool and no native tool, because the native names depend on the client. Claude Code serves them under the name its config gives the server, such as `mcp__figma-remote__use_figma`. Codex serves them through the Figma app on the ChatGPT account as `figma.use_figma`, and `codex exec` refuses that call with "MCP tool call requires approval" until the client's config approves app tools. That refusal is a client setting and not a Figma outage.

- List the connected tools first and use the names and input fields the server reports. Once a board's `fileKey` is known, on a new board, a revision or a read of a board written earlier, call `create_session` with it and pass the returned session id on every later call for this work. The route needs `use_figma` and `get_figjam`, and a new board also needs `whoami` and `create_new_file`. Load Figma's `figma-use` and `figma-use-figjam` skills before the first `use_figma` call, as Figma requires, and pass their names in `skillNames`. Flow Mode's rules win where the two differ
- Name the plan before the gate, because an account can hold plans that belong to other organizations. Call `whoami` and read the plans it returns. `whoami` says which plans the account holds and not which plan owns a board, so a plan it returns settles a new file only. On a new file one plan is named in the gate, and several plans become one question about which team the board belongs to, asked before the gate. A revision writes into a board whose plan was set when it was made, so on a revision the gate names the board and states its plan only when the user supplied it
- A new board starts with `create_new_file`, after the yes, with `editorType` set to `figjam`, `planKey` set to the plan the gate named and `fileName` set to the board's title. Load Figma's own skill for that tool first where the server offers one. Every later diagram of the same work and every revision passes that file's `fileKey`, so the work stays on one board
- Compose each diagram with `python3 scripts/compose_board.py <model file> --diagram <n> --out <code file>`, run on the model file the check passed and writing outside the repository. Exit 0 prints a `COMPOSED` line with the counts the read-back will look for and the name of the design the board is drawn in. Each design warning prints a `DESIGN` line before it and the `COMPOSED` line counts them: a token that cannot stand draws its shipped value, and a design file that cannot be read draws the shipped design whole. Exit 1 means the model fails the check, or the code runs past the 50,000 characters one call takes, and the failure line then says how many of them a team design's `THEME` takes. Either is fixed by splitting the diagram, never by trimming the code. Paste the code file's text unchanged as the `use_figma` code, one diagram per call
- The call returns the board id, the tag, the counts drawn beside the counts the model expects, every node and connector it drew with its id, any warnings and a screenshot of the whole board. A warning is a finding, reported as measured like a read-back mismatch
- A new board lands 400 pixels to the right of everything already on the page, its top level with the highest node there, so it never covers existing content and the diagrams of one piece of work read left to right in the order they were written
- The composer tags the board section it draws with shared plugin data under the fixed namespace `productowner`, keyed by the board's title, with the write time and the counts as the value. The title is the key because a later session can rebuild it, and it cannot rebuild an earlier run id. The tag carries nothing from the source material beyond the title the board already shows, because any plugin that can open the board can read shared plugin data. A refused tag becomes a warning and the board stands
- The tag departs from Figma's rule to keep workflow state outside the Figma file, because Flow Mode writes no file of its own, so the board is the only place a later session can learn what an earlier one wrote
- A failed or timed-out call is not proof that nothing landed. When `use_figma` reports `safeToRetryWithoutCanvasRead: true`, fix the error and retry once. Otherwise read the file with `get_figjam` before a retry, and retry only when the board is absent
- Read the written board back with `get_figjam`, as Section 7 sets out. When the server reports no read tool, the read-back is not possible and the reply says so. A read refused because the Starter plan or the View or Collab seat has spent its six tool calls for the month gives `Read-back: not possible` with that limit named, and the board is never called done
- Never move or restyle a composed node afterwards. Additions follow `references/hybrid-workflow.md`
- The rollback for a new file is that file. The rollback for an existing board is to delete the one board section the write returned, which removes everything drawn inside it, through `use_figma` and only on a reply that names it or a yes to a question that names it, as the delete rule below sets out. A later session finds the boards an earlier one wrote by reading the tag on every section at the top of the page, `figma.currentPage.children.filter((n) => n.type === 'SECTION' && n.getSharedPluginDataKeys('productowner').length)`. Stop if the section to delete carries no returned id and no tag. With no read tool nothing is deleted, and the user removes the board by hand
- A revision request reads the board with `get_figjam` first, so a change made since the last write is seen, then opens with a playback of the rows it changes, which waits for its answer before the gate. It composes the new board first, reads it back and then asks whether to delete the old board section found by its tag. When the new board keeps the old title, both sections carry the same tag key, so the old one is the tagged section with the earlier write time and the delete question names that time beside the title. The delete waits for its own yes to a question that names the old board by its title, so the yes that covered the compose never covers the delete, and with no second yes both boards stay. Composing first means a failed write never leaves the user with no board at all, and the tag means a revision in a new session replaces a board rather than drawing a second one beside it
- A delete of anything that was on the file before this write runs only on a reply that names the boards it removes, or on a yes to a question that names exactly those boards by title. A bare "yes" or "go ahead", the gate's yes and an answer to a question that named no board never delete such a board. The question lists every board the delete removes, and the delete removes those and no other. A board this conversation did not write, whether an earlier session or another person wrote it, is deleted only when the user's request is about that board, such as a revision of it, and never to tidy the page. Rolling back what this write added is not such a delete: it follows the rollback rule above, or the extension rollback in `references/hybrid-workflow.md`, each on its own yes to the deletion
- A board that holds two or more diagrams is planned before the first write, as `references/hybrid-workflow.md` Section 8 sets out

### Generated route, fallback

When `use_figma` is not among the connected tools and `generate_diagram` is, Figma's generator draws the diagram from the Mermaid block instead. Its board is plainer: the generator sets its own font, colours and layout, draws no title, zone or key and strips every `%%` line, so the title, subtitle, source and zone lines do not reach it. Figma marks `generate_diagram` as remote only, so a session connected only to Figma's desktop server has no `generate_diagram` and falls to the `fj` route or to No route. Load Figma's own diagram skill first where the runtime offers it.

- Send one diagram per call, with `name` set to a distinct title that matches its hand-off, `mermaidSyntax` set to the block and `userIntent` set to the reader's question in one sentence. An architecture also passes `useArchitectureLayoutCode` as `"FIGMA_DIAGRAM_2026"`, and no other type passes it
- The first call carries no `fileKey`, so the tool creates a new file. Every later diagram of the same work and every revision passes that file's `fileKey`. Never call a separate create-file tool first on this route
- Read the diagram back with `get_figjam` by label, as Section 7 sets out for a board with no layer names. A failed or timed-out call is read before a retry, and when the first call failed there is no `fileKey` to read, so ask the user to look for a new file in their FigJam drafts before a retry
- This route adds nothing beside the diagram, because a title, a tag, a note and a deletion all need `use_figma`. The gate says so, and the reply names the missing tool. The rollback for a new file is that file, and on an existing board the user removes the diagram by hand

### `fj` route, fallback

`figma-ds-cli` writes node by node into the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. It needs version 1.2.0 or later from the silships repository, because the npm build has no `fj` group, and its local daemon running. The vendored `mcp-figma/SKILL.md` owns the connection, the daemon and the mutating gate.

- The route draws a user flow, and a process with no lanes that uses only the user-flow shapes. Every other type needs a hosted route, because `fj` has no layout, container or table verb. It draws the diagram alone, with no title, zone or key
- On this route the target file is the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. Confirm with the read-only `fj info` that it is a FigJam board before the first write, and name it in the gate. Every FigJam verb fails on a design file
- `fj shape` per node: `--type ELLIPSE` for a start or end, `RECTANGLE` for a step, `DIAMOND` for a decision and a small `ELLIPSE` for a merge dot. Every position is computed, because `fj` has no layout verb
- `fj connect` per edge. It takes no label, so each edge label is its own `fj text` node beside the connector
- Read node ids back with `fj nodes -l` between steps when a create verb prints none, and read the finished diagram the same way. Each edge label is an `fj text` node, which the read-back counts as a label, never as a node
- `fj delete` and `fj eval` stay off this path. Each needs an explicit request and the destructive ceremony in `mcp-figma/`
- The rollback is Undo in the session, or a restore from the file's version history. A FigJam file has one page, so there is no page to duplicate first

### No route

A missing route changes only the write. The intake and the playback run as usual. The gate names the missing route in place of the plan and the calls, so its yes is to the missing-route reply. When no route is reachable, or the type needs a hosted route and neither `use_figma` nor `generate_diagram` is connected, that reply says which one is missing and what it needs, and for a type the `fj` route cannot draw it says so. Offer the checked model in the reply for the user to keep. With no Figma route, never claim a board exists and print no `Read-back:` line, because nothing was written. Never render the diagram as an image, an HTML page or a Mermaid file as a stand-in for the board.

When the type is one the `fj` route draws, a user flow or a process with no lanes, and `figma-ds-cli` is missing or not connected, the reply also names its setup. The vendored `../mcp-figma/` packet owns these steps and their scripts:

1. Install it once with `bash mcp-figma/scripts/install.sh` from the repository root, then confirm `figma-ds-cli --version` prints 1.2.0 or later
2. Import the bridge once: in Figma Desktop, choose Plugins, then Development, then Import plugin from manifest, and pick `~/.figma-ds-cli/source/plugin/manifest.json`, where the install puts it. The folder is hidden, so on macOS press Cmd+Shift+G in the file picker and paste the path
3. In each session, open the target FigJam file, run Plugins, then Development, then FigCli, keep it open, and connect with `figma-ds-cli connect --safe`

Never suggest the plain `figma-ds-cli connect`, which patches Figma Desktop, unless the user asks for it and has heard its rollback, `figma-ds-cli unpatch`. For a type only a hosted route draws, name the Figma MCP connection instead, because the `fj` route cannot draw it once set up.

---

## 7. READ-BACK

Each type's reference names what its read-back counts. Every read-back compares the board with the model, never with memory:

- Every node, state, participant, entity or task, by count and by label
- Every connector, message, transition or relationship, joining the same two ends in the same direction with the same label
- What the type adds, such as labelled decision exits, lanes, attributes or milestones

Direction comes from the connector, never from its position on the board. The two endpoint ids say which node each end attaches to. The two end caps say which way the arrow points. An arrow at the end is forward, an arrow at the start is reversed, an arrow at both ends is two-way and no arrow is undirected. A connector that reads reversed or two-way where the model drew one direction is a mismatch. So is a connector whose two ends are swapped. An ER connector is the exception, because a relationship has no direction. The composer marks each end with Figma's crow's-foot cap for its cardinality, `ERD_EXACTLY_ONE`, `ERD_ZERO_OR_ONE`, `ERD_ZERO_OR_MORE` or `ERD_ONE_OR_MORE`, and writes both ends into the label, such as `holds (1 to 0..n)`, with a solid line for an identifying relationship and a dashed one otherwise. A mark is not an arrow and sets no direction, so the connector is compared on its two ends, the mark at each end against its label, its label and its line. On the generated route no live read has yet shown the generator drawing cardinality markers, so an ER connector whose caps read plain there is counted on its two ends and its label alone.

A connector with a missing end, or an end pinned to the page or the canvas rather than to a node, is a mismatch named as dangling. It is never matched by its position.

On the composed route the read is `get_figjam` on the board id the write returned. It reports each section by name, each shape with its label text and each connector with its layer name and its two endpoint ids, so the board is matched to the model by name and by id. It returns no connector label text, so connector labels are matched from the composing write's own return and the overview screenshot:

- A node is a shape whose id the write returned in its node list, carrying the label the model gives it. Shapes inside the `Key` section are samples, and the empty 16 pixel ellipses are anchors that hold a routed connector, so neither counts as a node
- A connector is a connector named `edge:<from>-><to>`, one per model edge. A routed edge reaches its target through anchors, so its start is an anchor rather than the source: follow the connectors named `leg:<from>-><to>:<n>`, from the highest `<n>` down to `:1`, back through their anchors to the source node. The label sits on the leg that carries it
- A sequence message is named `edge:<from>-><to>:<n>`, with its order as the last part. Its ends hold anchors on the two lifelines rather than the participant boxes, so the name carries both parties and the screenshot shows the line between them
- A zone is a section named after its label, and its nodes sit inside it

On the generated route the read is `get_figjam`, node by node, matching shapes by their label because the generator writes no layer names. On the `fj` route it is `fj nodes -l`. When only a screenshot could be read, the read was visual, because a picture cannot prove which nodes a connector joins.

Every screenshot the read-back judges was rendered after the write it checks. The composing call's own screenshot is taken after its write by construction. A later write, such as a note, a revision or a hand fix the user asked for, is checked with `node.screenshot()` on the board inside a `use_figma` call, because `get_screenshot` has returned a board as it stood before the last write. A view that matches the board before the write is reported `stale`, taken again the same way and only then judged.

A board that already holds content can be slower to read than a fresh one. A read that times out is retried on fewer nodes at a time, halving the count until the read returns. A timeout is never proof that a node or a connector is missing. When the file held content before the write, the read-back reads those nodes again and compares their count, position and size with the read taken before the write, so the reply can say the content already there was left as it was.

---

## 8. DELIVERY

The reply carries the board, its proof and the self-scan, and nothing else. Anything the user must know or answer has a place above the self-scan.

- Everything written after the last tool call is the reply, and its first characters are the board URL. No sentence comes before it, not a heading, a summary, a note, a status line or a sentence announcing the reply, such as "The board is written and read back, so I'm sending the delivery reply now." The reply after a delete keeps this shape: it opens on the URL of the board that stays and repeats the `Left out:` line when the board has one
- The second line is the read-back, counts measured on the board against the model, in the words the type's reference uses: `Read-back: 8 of 8 nodes, 8 of 8 connectors, 2 of 2 decision exits labelled`. When a board was written and the connected tools include no read tool, the line is `Read-back: not possible, the connector has no read tool`, and the board is never called done. When the board URL landed in a re-saved artifact, the line ends with the name of the file the artifact was saved to. On a matched read-back the same line also names the first glance in one clause, such as `, first glance: the failed payment`, so the user knows what should win before the board is opened. On a revision whose changed end is the second glance, the next clause names it, such as `, second glance: the exception request`
- When the write added extensions, the next line counts them: `Extensions: 4 of 4 pins, 4 of 4 legend stickies, 0 overlaps`, or `Extensions: 2 of 2 notes, 0 overlaps` for single stickies
- When the board does not hold something the request or the sources named, a cut, a split into a second diagram, a flow left for a later board or a point the sources left open, the next line names each one as `Left out: <item>, <reason>`, whether or not the provenance table lists it, so the user sees what the board does not hold. On a split or a cut, the reason names the detail level and the cut, such as `Left out: the retry path, split into a second diagram`, and a split is named this way even when both boards sit in the same file
- A contradicted item appears in that same line with both of its sources and the reason it was not drawn, so a finding the sources disagree on is still visible to the reader
- When the file holds two or more diagrams, the read-back line also names the board a reader opens first, by the ordinal and the name in its title, in one clause such as `, start here: 1. Sign up`
- A finding from the read-back, a warning the write returned, a `DESIGN` line the composer printed, an open item or a question the user must answer is one `Finding:` line each, placed above the self-scan. A `DESIGN` finding names the token, what the design file asked for and the value the board drew instead. Where the board landed, the tools used, the cleanup and the rollback are not part of the reply
- The last line is the HVR self-scan in the shape `AGENTS.md` step 8 sets, counted on the labels written to the board. Nothing follows it, not a note, a finding or a question. Flow Mode is exempt from the export steps, never from the scan
- A read-back that does not match is reported as measured, with the missing or extra items named. The board is never called done on a mismatch
- A paired request, a route carrying `then: "FLOW"`, delivers the artifact first under its own mode's protocol: written, exported and read back. That reply ends on Flow Mode's playback, which waits for its own answer, with no ClickUp offer. Flow Mode then runs with that artifact as its product-doc source, under its own pre-write check and its own yes at the write gate
- When the request came with an artifact and the read-back matched the model, a Task, Bug, Story or Epic uses its `Flows` group and a Doc uses `Related references`, with the diagram’s name as the link text. The paired-output route and link placement are owned here
- The artifact is then saved again at its existing export path and read back, so the file the user keeps carries the link. That save is the artifact's own export step, not a Flow Mode one
- When only a screenshot could be read, the read-back line ends with `, read visually`. Connector labels, which `get_figjam` never returns, are counted from the write's return and the screenshot, so a labelled count on the line rests on those two and never ends it with `, read visually`. A label counted from the text a `get_figjam` read returned was read, not read visually, so the line never ends that way when the read returned the labels
- No file is written to `export/`, and no Mermaid, HTML, SVG or PNG file is left behind. The check and the composer read and write one scratch folder outside the repository, which the clean-up step deletes before the reply is sent. Create the scratch folder with `mktemp -d` and keep its path in the conversation, never in a fixed file

### The playback

Each round of intake opens with a short replay of the rows settled so far, one row per line, each in the words the product uses. The replay sits above the round's next question, so a wrong row is corrected before more answers build on it.

Before the model there is one full playback, and it waits for one answer. It states the Brief's question and its outcome, the detail level, the audience and the distance by their words, what each source settled, every row still open and every fact it assumed. That answer is not the gate's yes, because the gate asks about a write and the playback asks about the reading.

An unanswered question never stops the work. The reading proceeds on the recommendation the question gave, the fact is marked assumed and the playback names it, so the user corrects it before anything is written. A yes moves the work on to the model. A correction changes that row and the playback runs again over the rows it touched.

The playback is not one of the five reply lines. It runs before the write, and the reply states only the board, the read-back, the extensions, what was left out and the self-scan.

### The gate is its own reply

The playback and the gate are two replies, never one. Each is the last message of its turn: the turn ends on the stop's question, never on a status line after it, and a stop is never posted as a message in the middle of a turn that goes on working. An intake round ends the same way, on the closing question `assets/flow-templates.md` Section 5 puts after its last block. None of the three carries the `HVR self-scan:` line, which belongs to the reply that delivers the board, because a stop delivers nothing. The playback comes before the model, so its reply carries no Mermaid, no check result and no composed code. It ends on its one question about the reading, names no plan, lists no calls and never asks whether to write. The gate reply follows the playback's answer, and its one question asks about the write alone. No question is ever worded so that one yes covers both, such as a yes that confirms the reading and the write together.

Only a yes to the gate's own question writes. A yes to the playback, an answer to an intake round, a request to use the recommended answers or a yes to a question no reply asked never writes. Before the playback has had its answer, the reply to any of those is the playback. Once it has, and the gate has not been shown yet, the reply is the gate, and the write waits for the yes that answers it. A request to use the recommended answers sent after the playback counts as the playback's answer.

---

## 9. ERROR RECOVERY

### The check fails

Fix the named rule, or split the diagram at a natural hand-off, and run the check again. Never write a model the check failed.

### The type or the order is ambiguous

Ask one question naming the two types or the two orders that fit, then wait.

### The read-back differs from the model

Report the measured counts and the items that differ. To replace the board, compose it again with the same `fileKey` and read the new board back. Then ask whether to delete the old board section found by its tag, naming it by its title, and delete it only on that second yes, because a second board beside the first duplicates it. The yes that covered the compose never covers the delete. In a later session, read the tags before anything is deleted or recomposed. The tag's key is the board's title, so a later session rebuilds the key without knowing the earlier run id, and the new board replaces the old one instead of sitting beside it. With no read tool, the user removes the old board by hand first. After two attempts at the same board, stop and ask what is wrong rather than composing again, and offer in that question that the board can be edited by hand in FigJam.

### A node needs moving, resizing or restyling

Flow Mode never edits a composed node in place. A change the model can carry is made in the model and the board is composed again after a yes: the direction, the zones, the declaration order, the edge set, a `style` line that marks a decision, a failure or the step in focus, a `%% goal:` line that names the goal, and the title, subtitle and source lines. The old board section is then deleted only on its own second yes, asked after the new board is read back. A change to how every board looks, such as which colour a kind takes, the accent, the type sizes or the key's words, is a change to `assets/figjam-design.md` and never to one board, so the reply names that file and the token, and the boards composed after the edit follow it. A change the model cannot carry, such as a custom colour, another font on one board or a nudge to one node, is a hand edit in FigJam. The reply says so plainly instead of attempting it, and names the node by its label so it is easy to find. On the generated route nothing can be restyled, so every change to the look is a hand edit, and a change to what the diagram says is fixed by generating it again from the model.

### A Figma tool seems missing

List the connected tools in this turn before saying a route is missing. Some clients connect the Figma server after the session starts, so a tool that is absent from the first listing is listed once more before the reply names it missing. A route is never called missing, dropped or disconnected from memory or from an earlier turn, and the reply that says so names the listing that showed it.

### `use_figma` fails to connect

`use_figma` answers a call that carries no `fileKey` with "Failed to connect to MCP server 'figma'", which reads like an outage. Before calling the route down or falling back, check that the failing call carried the `fileKey` the gate named, and retry once with it. A call with no `fileKey` never reached the file, so this retry needs no `get_figjam` read first, unlike the failed call Section 6 sets out. Only a retry with the key that fails the same way counts as a connection failure, and the reply that says so names both calls.

### An extension fails

The diagram stands. Report what landed and what did not, as `references/hybrid-workflow.md` Section 7 sets out.

### The plan or file is unclear

Stop before the write and ask. A board in the wrong plan is visible to that plan's members as soon as it lands. Where the server reports a `whoami` tool, call it before asking, because it returns the plans the account holds. On a new file a single plan resolves the gap and the gate names it. More than one plan means one question about which team the board belongs to. On a revision the board keeps the plan it was made in, so the gate names the board and states its plan only when the user supplied it.

These lines are the whole reply, and the self-scan is always the last. Each finding, warning, open item or question is one `Finding:` line, and nothing follows the self-scan. The playback of the settled rows runs before the model and the gate, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 8 sets out, and it never becomes a line here.

Everything written after the last tool call is the reply, so its first characters are the board URL and no sentence comes before it, not even one that says the board is written or that the reply follows.

- Wrong first line: `The board is written and read back, so I'm sending the delivery reply now.`
- Right first line: the board URL, alone

---

## 5. INTAKE QUESTIONS

The type table in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3 reads as questions. Ask them as an interview before the model is written, in three rounds that depend on each other, because an answer in one round settles what the next round may ask.

| Round | Asks | Settles |
|---|---|---|
| One | The reader, the question, the outcome and the three dials | Who the board is for, what it must answer, what the reader decides next and the detail level, the audience and the reading distance `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets |
| Two | Entry, exit and actors | Where the flow starts, where it ends and who takes each step |
| Three | Decisions, states, sources and class | Where the flow branches, which states exist, which source states each fact and what class that source holds |

When two types fit, or a type the user names does not fit what the brief describes, the type question is asked alone in the first reply, before round one, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3 sets out.

### Every question carries a reading and a recommendation

A user who does not know an answer should still be able to accept one, so every question is put in this shape:

```text
Reading: <what the sources already show for this question>
Question: <the one thing still open>
Recommended: <the answer the AI would take>
Why: <the one line of reason>
```

- One to three questions per round and no later round while an earlier one is open
- A round ends on one closing question after its last block, such as `Take the recommended answers, or correct any of them?`, so each Why line stays inside its block
- Never a question a supplied source already answers, because that answer is stated as the reading instead
- A round closes when each of its questions is answered, accepted or corrected

### A vague answer is asked again

An answer that names nothing is asked once more with one probe from this set, and never with the same wording twice:

- A concrete scenario, such as one example walked from the first click to the end
- An edge case, such as two of these arriving at once
- A contradiction, such as one source stating this and another stating the opposite
- A term, such as what one word means in this product
- A scale, such as how many of these exist on a busy day
- A failure mode, such as what the reader sees when one step fails
- A boundary, such as where this flow stops and another one begins

### An unanswered question is never a dead end

When the user skips a question or says they do not know, the AI takes the recommended answer. That fact is marked assumed in the Brief and named in the playback before the gate, so the user corrects it before anything is written. A recommendation the user accepts without supplying a source stays assumed, with what would settle it, and the playback names it. A row the user corrects is recorded as `corrected` and counts as settled. No later round asks it again.

3	description: "Human Voice hard blockers carried inline, loaded on every request so the banned terms are in view while writing."

12	
13	# Rules - Human Voice Core
14	
15	Human Voice hard blockers carried inline, loaded on every request so the banned terms are in view while writing.
16	
17	**Loading Condition:** ALWAYS
18	**Purpose:** Carries the Human Voice hard blockers inline so the banned terms are in view on every request, without loading the full standard
19	**Scope:** Punctuation, hard blocker words and phrases, banned metaphors and cliches, setup language, generalisation fixes, output warnings, structural bans, always-cut modifiers and the before-delivery self-scan report line
20	**Output Path:** None. The card governs the wording of an artifact another file writes, and produces none of its own
21	**Authority:** `Rules - Human Voice - EN` is the full standard, symlinked into every consuming system as its own human-voice reference. Carried here: punctuation, hard blocker words and phrases, banned metaphors, setup phrases, generalisation fixes, output warnings, structural bans, always-cut modifiers. Left there: soft deductions, context-dependent flags, voice directives, the precedence hierarchy and the point scoring. Load the standard ON_DEMAND to settle a borderline term or run a scored pass.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 1. OVERVIEW
26	
27	### Purpose
28	
29	A hard blocker is a failure, not a deduction. An always-cut edit carries no penalty. Only hard blockers are counted on the self-scan line.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. PUNCTUATION, NEVER
34	
35	Em dash `—`, semicolon `;`, Oxford comma, asterisk emphasis in delivered output, curly quotes (use straight `"` and `'`), title-case headings (use sentence case). Maximum one ellipsis and one emoji per piece. Bullet items never end with a full stop.
36	
37	### System-granted exemptions
38	
39	A consuming system may grant a narrow exemption where a target format fixes a shape this section bans, and only inside the exact shape it names. An exemption is granted by that system's own surfaces, never assumed from this card, and it never widens to other prose. Every granted exemption is listed below with the system and the shape that earns it, so a shape absent from this list stays banned. Preserved source text in a refinement keeps the punctuation it arrived with.
40	
41	- Product Owner Doc Mode grants the ClickUp definition delimiter `*   **Term** — definition` in a new ClickUp document
42	- Product Owner Doc Mode grants the status-label delimiter `Status: {source class} — {scope or qualifier}`, in a document-wide status notice and in a section-level or entry-level status line, because the qualifier itself routinely carries commas
43	- Product Owner Doc Mode grants the Catalog entry delimiter `### {Stable ID} — {Entry name}` on an H3 entry heading and on its `*   [{Stable ID} — {Entry name}](#{entry-anchor})` index link, inside a Catalog that carries its Index heading, and nowhere else
44	- Product Owner Bug Mode grants the two fixed corpus labels `**1. Observed Behavior**` and `**2. Expected Behavior**`, which the Barter bug corpus writes verbatim. No other heading or label in that system escapes sentence case
45	- Product Owner Story Mode grants the literal placeholder `TBD...` in the three `## Delivery` slots, Estimation, Rabbit holes and No-gos. It is a fixed token rather than a prose ellipsis, so it never counts against the one-ellipsis cap
46	- Barter Deal Templates grants one closing emoji per headline and one trailing emoji at the end of each offer, value, creator-fit and requirement bullet line in deal copy. None may lead a line or sit in About prose, and every other piece that system writes keeps the one-emoji cap
47	
48	---
49	
50	## 3. HARD BLOCKER WORDS
51	
52	delve, embark, realm, tapestry, illuminate, unveil, elucidate, abyss, revolutionise, game-changer, groundbreaking, cutting-edge, ever-evolving, shed light, dive deep, leverage, foster, nurture, resonate, empower, disrupt, curate, harness, elevate, robust, seamless, holistic, synergy, unpack, paradigm, enlightening, esteemed, remarkable, skyrocket, skyrocketing, utilize, utilizing
53	
54	Blocked as metaphor, allowed when literal: navigating, landscape, unlock, ecosystem, journey, deep dive.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## 4. HARD BLOCKER PHRASES
59	
60	"It's important to", "It's worth noting", "It goes without saying", "At the end of the day", "Moving forward", "In today's world", "In today's digital landscape", "When it comes to", "Dive into", "I'd love to", "Navigating the [X]", "That being said", "Having said that", "Let me be clear", "The reality is", "Here's the thing", "In a world where", "You're not alone", "The real question is", "Here's what you need to know", "What most people don't realise is", "The truth is"
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 5. BANNED METAPHORS AND CLICHES
65	
66	"bridge the gap", "tip of the iceberg", "pave the way", "a world where", "the landscape of", "at the heart of", "double-edged sword", "game-changer", "move the needle", "low-hanging fruit", "think outside the box", "raise the bar", "level the playing field", "a perfect storm", "the elephant in the room", "a deep dive", "the bottom line", "food for thought", "a breath of fresh air", "light at the end of the tunnel"
67	
68	Delete the figure and write the literal thing: the specific change, the specific metric, the specific trade-off, the specific factors.
69	
70	---
71	
72	## 6. SETUP LANGUAGE
73	
74	Filler that announces what is coming instead of saying it. Say the thing.
75	
76	"In conclusion", "In summary", "It's worth noting", "It's important to note", "Let's explore", "Let's dive in", "Let's take a look", "When it comes to", "In the world of", "In today's [X]", "At its core", "At the end of the day", "Without further ado", "As we all know", "It goes without saying", "First and foremost", "Last but not least", "With that in mind", "On that note", "That said"
77	
78	---
79	
80	## 7. GENERALISATION FIXES
81	
82	"Many companies", "Studies show", "Experts agree", "In recent years", "A growing number of", "Research suggests", "Industry leaders", "Across industries", "Time and again", "Some people"
83	
84	Replace each with the verifiable claim: name the company, the study and year, the expert, the timeframe, the number, the institution, the industries, who and how often.
85	
86	---
87	
88	## 8. OUTPUT WARNINGS
89	
90	These govern the written artifact. Nothing below belongs inside a deliverable.
91	
92	- No meta-commentary about the writing process
93	- No disclaimers or notes about tone choices
94	- No reference to these rules
95	- No explanation of why a word was avoided or replaced
96	- No lines such as "I've kept this concise" or "I avoided jargon"
97	- No knowledge-cutoff disclaimers or date hedging ("as of my last update", "based on available information", "while specific details are limited")
98	- No training-data hedging ("Up to my last training update", "I don't have access to real-time data")
99	
100	---
101	
102	## 9. STRUCTURAL BANS, WHAT NO SCANNER SEES
103	
104	- **"Not just X, but Y."** Every variant, "not only X but Y" included. State X. State Y separately
105	- **Triad density, never the triad itself.** A single three-item list is fine and needs no defence. What this flags is two or more of them inside 150 words, which reads as a tic. Fix that by merging or splitting a list whose content genuinely allows it, and prefer counts of 2, 4 or 5 where the count is yours to choose. Never invent a filler item, and never drop a real one, to move a count off three. A triad the source, the template or the subject fixes (a three-slot taxonomy, a three-value enum, three named states) is content, and padding it is a worse failure than the tic this rule exists to catch
106	- **Copula avoidance.** "serves as", "stands as", "functions as", "acts as", "boasts", "features", "offers". Write "is" or "has"
107	- **Synonym cycling.** Reaching for a second word for a thing you already named, so the prose looks varied. Pick one term and repeat it every time. Repeating a fixed label, an identifier or a template's own wording is this rule being obeyed, never a violation of it
108	- **False ranges.** "From X to Y" where the endpoints share no scale
109	- **Inline-header vertical lists.** A stack of bolded-header bullets in the bold-plus-colon shape. Rewrite as prose or a plain list. Allowed in glossaries, API docs and config guides
110	- **Generic conclusions.** "the future looks bright", "exciting times lie ahead", "a major step forward", "the possibilities are endless", "we look forward to what's next", "this is just the beginning", "the best is yet to come", "continue their journey toward excellence". End on a specific, or end
111	- **Fragmented headers.** A first sentence restating its heading. Cut it, open on substance
112	- **Significance inflation.** "marks a pivotal moment in", "setting the stage for", "indelible mark", "is a testament to", "underscores the importance of", "reflects broader trends in", "represents a shift in", "key turning point", "shaping the future of", "deeply rooted in", "symbolising its ongoing", "contributing to the". State what happened, then the evidence

# Rules - Human Voice Core

Human Voice hard blockers carried inline, loaded on every request so the banned terms are in view while writing.

**Loading Condition:** ALWAYS
**Purpose:** Carries the Human Voice hard blockers inline so the banned terms are in view on every request, without loading the full standard
**Scope:** Punctuation, hard blocker words and phrases, banned metaphors and cliches, setup language, generalisation fixes, output warnings, structural bans, always-cut modifiers and the before-delivery self-scan report line
**Output Path:** None. The card governs the wording of an artifact another file writes, and produces none of its own
**Authority:** `Rules - Human Voice - EN` is the full standard, symlinked into every consuming system as its own human-voice reference. Carried here: punctuation, hard blocker words and phrases, banned metaphors, setup phrases, generalisation fixes, output warnings, structural bans, always-cut modifiers. Left there: soft deductions, context-dependent flags, voice directives, the precedence hierarchy and the point scoring. Load the standard ON_DEMAND to settle a borderline term or run a scored pass.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

A hard blocker is a failure, not a deduction. An always-cut edit carries no penalty. Only hard blockers are counted on the self-scan line.

---

## 2. PUNCTUATION, NEVER

Em dash `—`, semicolon `;`, Oxford comma, asterisk emphasis in delivered output, curly quotes (use straight `"` and `'`), title-case headings (use sentence case). Maximum one ellipsis and one emoji per piece. Bullet items never end with a full stop.

### System-granted exemptions

A consuming system may grant a narrow exemption where a target format fixes a shape this section bans, and only inside the exact shape it names. An exemption is granted by that system's own surfaces, never assumed from this card, and it never widens to other prose. Every granted exemption is listed below with the system and the shape that earns it, so a shape absent from this list stays banned. Preserved source text in a refinement keeps the punctuation it arrived with.

- Product Owner Doc Mode grants the ClickUp definition delimiter `*   **Term** — definition` in a new ClickUp document
- Product Owner Doc Mode grants the status-label delimiter `Status: {source class} — {scope or qualifier}`, in a document-wide status notice and in a section-level or entry-level status line, because the qualifier itself routinely carries commas
- Product Owner Doc Mode grants the Catalog entry delimiter `### {Stable ID} — {Entry name}` on an H3 entry heading and on its `*   [{Stable ID} — {Entry name}](#{entry-anchor})` index link, inside a Catalog that carries its Index heading, and nowhere else
- Product Owner Bug Mode grants the two fixed corpus labels `**1. Observed Behavior**` and `**2. Expected Behavior**`, which the Barter bug corpus writes verbatim. No other heading or label in that system escapes sentence case
- Product Owner Story Mode grants the literal placeholder `TBD...` in the three `## Delivery` slots, Estimation, Rabbit holes and No-gos. It is a fixed token rather than a prose ellipsis, so it never counts against the one-ellipsis cap
- Barter Deal Templates grants one closing emoji per headline and one trailing emoji at the end of each offer, value, creator-fit and requirement bullet line in deal copy. None may lead a line or sit in About prose, and every other piece that system writes keeps the one-emoji cap

---

## 3. HARD BLOCKER WORDS

delve, embark, realm, tapestry, illuminate, unveil, elucidate, abyss, revolutionise, game-changer, groundbreaking, cutting-edge, ever-evolving, shed light, dive deep, leverage, foster, nurture, resonate, empower, disrupt, curate, harness, elevate, robust, seamless, holistic, synergy, unpack, paradigm, enlightening, esteemed, remarkable, skyrocket, skyrocketing, utilize, utilizing

Blocked as metaphor, allowed when literal: navigating, landscape, unlock, ecosystem, journey, deep dive.

---

## 4. HARD BLOCKER PHRASES

"It's important to", "It's worth noting", "It goes without saying", "At the end of the day", "Moving forward", "In today's world", "In today's digital landscape", "When it comes to", "Dive into", "I'd love to", "Navigating the [X]", "That being said", "Having said that", "Let me be clear", "The reality is", "Here's the thing", "In a world where", "You're not alone", "The real question is", "Here's what you need to know", "What most people don't realise is", "The truth is"

---

## 5. BANNED METAPHORS AND CLICHES

"bridge the gap", "tip of the iceberg", "pave the way", "a world where", "the landscape of", "at the heart of", "double-edged sword", "game-changer", "move the needle", "low-hanging fruit", "think outside the box", "raise the bar", "level the playing field", "a perfect storm", "the elephant in the room", "a deep dive", "the bottom line", "food for thought", "a breath of fresh air", "light at the end of the tunnel"

Delete the figure and write the literal thing: the specific change, the specific metric, the specific trade-off, the specific factors.

---

## 6. SETUP LANGUAGE

Filler that announces what is coming instead of saying it. Say the thing.

"In conclusion", "In summary", "It's worth noting", "It's important to note", "Let's explore", "Let's dive in", "Let's take a look", "When it comes to", "In the world of", "In today's [X]", "At its core", "At the end of the day", "Without further ado", "As we all know", "It goes without saying", "First and foremost", "Last but not least", "With that in mind", "On that note", "That said"

---

## 7. GENERALISATION FIXES

"Many companies", "Studies show", "Experts agree", "In recent years", "A growing number of", "Research suggests", "Industry leaders", "Across industries", "Time and again", "Some people"

Replace each with the verifiable claim: name the company, the study and year, the expert, the timeframe, the number, the institution, the industries, who and how often.

---

## 8. OUTPUT WARNINGS

These govern the written artifact. Nothing below belongs inside a deliverable.

- No meta-commentary about the writing process
- No disclaimers or notes about tone choices
- No reference to these rules
- No explanation of why a word was avoided or replaced
- No lines such as "I've kept this concise" or "I avoided jargon"
- No knowledge-cutoff disclaimers or date hedging ("as of my last update", "based on available information", "while specific details are limited")
- No training-data hedging ("Up to my last training update", "I don't have access to real-time data")

---

## 9. STRUCTURAL BANS, WHAT NO SCANNER SEES

- **"Not just X, but Y."** Every variant, "not only X but Y" included. State X. State Y separately
- **Triad density, never the triad itself.** A single three-item list is fine and needs no defence. What this flags is two or more of them inside 150 words, which reads as a tic. Fix that by merging or splitting a list whose content genuinely allows it, and prefer counts of 2, 4 or 5 where the count is yours to choose. Never invent a filler item, and never drop a real one, to move a count off three. A triad the source, the template or the subject fixes (a three-slot taxonomy, a three-value enum, three named states) is content, and padding it is a worse failure than the tic this rule exists to catch
- **Copula avoidance.** "serves as", "stands as", "functions as", "acts as", "boasts", "features", "offers". Write "is" or "has"
- **Synonym cycling.** Reaching for a second word for a thing you already named, so the prose looks varied. Pick one term and repeat it every time. Repeating a fixed label, an identifier or a template's own wording is this rule being obeyed, never a violation of it
- **False ranges.** "From X to Y" where the endpoints share no scale
- **Inline-header vertical lists.** A stack of bolded-header bullets in the bold-plus-colon shape. Rewrite as prose or a plain list. Allowed in glossaries, API docs and config guides
- **Generic conclusions.** "the future looks bright", "exciting times lie ahead", "a major step forward", "the possibilities are endless", "we look forward to what's next", "this is just the beginning", "the best is yet to come", "continue their journey toward excellence". End on a specific, or end
- **Fragmented headers.** A first sentence restating its heading. Cut it, open on substance
- **Significance inflation.** "marks a pivotal moment in", "setting the stage for", "indelible mark", "is a testament to", "underscores the importance of", "reflects broader trends in", "represents a shift in", "key turning point", "shaping the future of", "deeply rooted in", "symbolising its ongoing", "contributing to the". State what happened, then the evidence
- **Notability by association.** Listing three or more outlets without a specific claim, "active social media presence with over X followers", "has been featured in", "covered by major publications". Cite the specific coverage and what it said
- **Formulaic challenges sections.** "Despite its [quality], [subject] faces challenges typical of", "Despite these challenges, [subject] continues to thrive", "Challenges and Legacy", "Future Outlook", "faces several challenges, including". Give the specific facts

---

## 10. ALWAYS CUT

Always-cut edits, not scored penalties. Cut the word, keep the sentence. These are edits, so they never count toward the hard blocker total.

very, really, truly, absolutely, incredibly, extremely, quite, rather, somewhat, fairly, just, actually, basically, literally, simply, obviously, clearly, certainly, definitely, undoubtedly, essentially

Never cut a semantic connective (because, so, unless, which means) to save words.

---

## 11. BEFORE DELIVERY

Draft, reread as a skeptical human reader, fix, then report on the required line:

`HVR self-scan: N hard blockers. Fixed: <terms>. Kept with reason: <terms>.`

`N` counts hard blockers only: punctuation, blocker words, blocker phrases, metaphors, setup phrases, unfixed generalisations, output-warning leaks and structural bans. A literal use, such as a source's own relationship verb, is named with that reason and not counted.

It belongs in the response beside the export path, never inside the artifact body, exactly as a Mode, Template, Perspectives, Quality Score or Energy header stays out of a delivered artifact. That is why this card runs 5, 7, 8, 12 rather than counting straight, and why renumbering it would break the Section 8 citations three skills carry
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 1. THE TWO-SIDED CONTRACT
28	
29	Cuts and keeps here are edits rather than scored penalties, so they never count toward a system's hard blocker total. The two halves are load-bearing in equal measure: read only the cut half and the output arrives compressed until the reasoning falls out of it, and read only the keep half and nothing ever gets shorter. Every rule the validator blocks on arrives in a pair at the same strength, so the gate cannot be satisfied by cutting alone.
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. THE RECONSTRUCTION TEST
34	
35	After a cut, could a reader who does not already know the answer recover what was removed from what remains? If yes, the cut was free. If no, the information moved into the reader's head, which is loss wearing the shape of compression. Apply it per cut and never per document, because a document-level verdict is a judgement about length and length is the judgement that strips connectives. The reader it asks about is the one who opens the artifact three weeks later with no memory of the conversation that produced it.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## 3. CUT RULES
40	
41	### 3.1 The named rules
42	
43	- **Question echo.** An opening that restates the prompt before answering it
44	- **Intent narration.** Announcing the move instead of making it
45	- **Compliance acknowledgement.** Agreeing to do the work at the top of the work
46	- **Terminal recap.** A closing paragraph that repeats the body, even accurately
47	- **Hedge stack.** Two or more uncertainty markers on one claim. Keep the one that is true
48	- **Importance assertion.** A sentence whose only content is that something matters
49	- **The conclusion move.** The whole paragraph, not only the phrase that opens it
50	- **Both-sides padding.** Symmetric pro and con on a question that is not symmetric
51	- **Empty enumeration.** Naming that there are several things, listing them, analysing none
52	- **Heading echo.** A first sentence that restates its own heading
53	- **Restated constraint.** Repeating back a fact the user supplied
54	- **Effort reporting.** Narrating the work done rather than what it found
55	- **Count padding.** An item added so a list carries a different number of items. The triad rule counts triads per 150 words and bans none, so leave the count alone and cut something that was never load-bearing
56	
57	### 3.2 The stated vocabulary
58	
59	The validator blocks on exactly the terms below, so this list and the gate are one list, and adding a term to either alone is the drift that kept these checks advisory. Section 3.3 of the on-demand rationale records every candidate refused, with the correct writing each would have failed.
60	
61	Never open a sentence with: "In conclusion", "In summary", "To summarize", "To summarise", "To recap", "To sum up", "It's worth noting", "It is worth noting", "It's important to note", "It is important to note", "Let's explore", "Let's dive in", "Let's take a look", "At the end of the day", "Without further ado", "As we all know", "It goes without saying", "First and foremost", "Last but not least", "With that in mind", "On that note", "That said", "Needless to say", "Simply put", "In essence", "At its core", "In the world of", "When it comes to", "At a high level", "As you can see", "As mentioned above", "As noted above", "As previously noted", "As we have seen", "As discussed above", "In this section", "Put simply", "Generally speaking", "Broadly speaking", "The key takeaway", "The fact of the matter is", "It should be noted", "It must be noted", "By way of background".
62	
63	Never close a section on: "In summary", "In conclusion", "To summarize", "To summarise", "To recap", "To sum up", "In short", "All in all", "Overall", "Ultimately", "In closing", "To conclude", "To wrap up", "The takeaway", "Net net", "In a nutshell", "Long story short", "To put it simply", "On the whole".
64	
65	At most one hedge per claim: "might", "may", "could", "perhaps", "maybe", "possibly", "potentially", "probably", "seems", "appears", "arguably", "somewhat", "relatively", "presumably", "likely", "generally", "typically", "I think", "I believe", "tends to", "to some extent", "in some cases", "apparently", "conceivably", "ostensibly", "seemingly", "in theory", "I suspect", "My sense is".
66	
67	A cross-reference that names its target stays legitimate, so "As noted above" is banned while "the payout window defined under The weekly cycle" is not. A heading followed by a sentence that shares its words and adds no new one is a heading echo: cut the sentence and open on substance.
68	
69	### 3.4 The two cut rules the validator settles alone
70	
71	Both resolve without judgement, so the validator blocks on them in a deliverable and reports them as advice on an instruction file.
72	
73	**Importance assertion.** A sentence of twelve words or fewer carrying one of "important", "critical", "essential", "crucial", "vital", "matters", "significant", "noteworthy" or "fundamental", and carrying no content word of its own beyond that marker and generic filler. A sentence that names what matters and why is left alone.
74	
75	**Effort reporting.** A sentence opening on "I" or "We" that reaches one of "analysed", "analyzed", "reviewed", "checked", "scored", "scanned", "verified", "examined", "evaluated", "assessed", "investigated" or "audited" within the next few words. A quoted mention is left alone, and so is a sentence whose subject is the process the artifact documents rather than the author. State what the work found, since the work itself is not the deliverable.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 4. KEEP RULES
80	
81	The anti-robotic half, at the same weight as the cut list. Each item names what a compression pass destroys first.
82	
83	- **Semantic connectives.** `because`, `so`, `which means`, `unless`, `otherwise`, `since` carry the logic, and deleting one turns an argument into a pile of assertions. The Human Voice cap on `however`, `furthermore`, `moreover`, `additionally` and `consequently` limits rhetoric and never reaches these
84	- **One concrete instance per non-obvious rule.** The example is what makes a rule applicable
85	- **The caveat that prevents a wrong action.** A reader who follows the trimmed version and breaks something was not served by the trim
86	- **The scope qualifier.** `when`, `only when`, `for X but not Y`. A rule stripped of its scope is applied everywhere
87	- **The noun behind a pronoun.** Name it again once the referent sits more than a clause away
88	- **The negative case.** "A path string is not verification" is where the reader learns the boundary
89	- **The specific number.** 33 fixtures, not several fixtures
90	- **One human beat per roughly 400 words.** An aside, a judgement, a plain admission of what is unknown
91	- **Grammar.** Articles, copulas and finite verbs are never a compression target, because conciseness removes claims and never syntax
92	
93	---
94	
95	## 5. OVER-COMPRESSION SIGNATURES
96	
97	### 5.1 The five shapes
98	
99	- **Connective stripping.** Clauses sit next to each other with the relation deleted, so the reader guesses whether the second causes, qualifies or contradicts the first
100	- **Referent stripping.** Pronouns and bare nouns left with their antecedents cut away
101	- **Telegraphese.** Dropped articles and copulas, verbless fragments, headline grammar in body text
102	- **Condition collapse.** A conditional rule flattened into an absolute one, which is a correctness bug rather than a style one
103	- **Example deletion.** An abstract rule left with nothing showing what it looks like in use
104	
105	### 5.2 The two the validator counts, and the perimeter they are measured over
106	
107	Connective stripping and telegraphese leave a numeric trace, so the validator counts them and blocks on a deliverable below either floor. Repair a document that trips one by naming the deleted relations back in and restoring the subject behind every stranded pronoun, never by adding words.
108	
109	- **Connective floor.** At least 5 semantic connectives per 1000 words of prose
110	- **Article floor.** At least 30 articles per 1000 words of prose
111	
112	Both floors are measured over paragraph prose alone, because a ratio only means something where sentences carry the reasoning. Outside the perimeter: frontmatter, a heading at any level, a bullet, a numbered item, a table row, a blockquote, an image, a horizontal rule, a field line such as `**Placement:** Creator deals dashboard`, a hashtag or handle run, a label line whose whole content is one bold or underlined run such as `**Most authentic**`, anything inside a fenced code block, and any HTML comment. Below 200 words of paragraph prose neither floor is applied, since a ratio over fewer words than that is noise.
113	
114	---
115	
116	## 7. FORMAT
117	
118	Prose, bullets and tables are not interchangeable, and picking wrong is how a short answer still reads badly. Three questions decide and the first yes wins: prose where the items differ in weight or their order encodes reasoning, a table where every row shares the same fields, bullets where the items are parallel, independently actionable and three to seven in number. Anything reaching the end without a yes is one paragraph pretending to be a list. Over-bulleting is the main way output turns robotic while looking concise, and the tells are verbless fragments, a bullet that needs the one above it to parse, and a list whose connectives were deleted so the items would line up. Heading density scales with length: under 300 words no headings, above that one per 150 to 400 words.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## 8. WHAT A DELIVERABLE NEVER CONTAINS
123	
124	The reasoning that produced an artifact, the score it earned and the assumptions it rests on are real work, and they belong in the reply beside the export path rather than inside the file the reader opens.
125	
126	### 8.1 The enumeration
127	
128	- A scoring section of any kind, whether headed MEQT, HVR, DEAL scoring, Scoring, Self-scan, Hard blockers or Weakest
129	- A dimension breakdown line, such as `M 4 · E 6 · Q 6 · T 3 · D 3` or its `D · E · A · L` equivalent
130	- A total, a floor status, a pass or fail verdict, or a score band action
131	- A hard blocker count or a voice self-scan line, in any wording
132	- Score commentary, such as a line opening `Weakest:` and naming which dimensions were thin
133	- An improvement-cycle note, an iteration count or a re-score history
134	- A bracketed `[Assumes: ...]` tag
135	- A methodology transcript, a perspective roster, an energy level or a phase-flow trace
136	- A validation checklist, a gate roster or a template-compliance report
137	- An attestation footer, a Mode header in visible text, a Template version in visible text, or any other processing metadata
138	
139	### 8.2 The one sanctioned exception
140	
141	Line 1 may carry a single HTML comment header, which renders as nothing and is the designed home for the mode, the framework, the score and the template version. A `Stats:` or `Assumes:` line written as an HTML comment directly below sits inside the same exception, for the same reason. Invisible when rendered is the whole test, so a score written as visible text is a violation wherever it sits in the file and a score written as a comment is fine wherever it sits.
142	
143	### 8.3 Where the reporting goes instead
144	
145	The reply carries what the artifact does not: the export path with read-back confirmation where the runtime can write files, the score and its verdict at the depth the mode calls for, the voice self-scan line naming the terms fixed and the terms kept with their reason, the assumptions in a form the user can correct before they harden, a short summary and one next step. Producing that report is the point, and moving it out of the artifact does not make it optional.
146	
147	### 8.4 Two narrow overrides
148	
149	Where the artifact refines a supplied source, never inject a Mode, Template, Perspectives, Quality Score or Energy header into preserved source structure, since the comment header is for a new artifact and a refinement keeps the source's own opening. Where the packaging renders the deliverable in a panel instead of saving a file, that rendered block is the artifact and the enumeration applies to it unchanged, the report follows the block, and the path is reported as export-equivalent rather than claimed as a save.
150	
151	---
152	
153	## 12. THE PRE-EXPORT PASS
154	
155	Run this after the voice pass and before the export, in order. The first two steps are the cut side and the last three are the keep side, and running only the cut side is the failure this layer exists to prevent.
156	
157	1. Delete every opener, recap and hedge stack named in Section 3.2, both shapes named in Section 3.4, and the question echo, intent narration, compliance acknowledgement and closing recap the body already carries, including the sentences after the phrase that opened one
158	2. Apply the reconstruction test to every remaining cut you are tempted to make, and stop at the first one that fails
159	3. Name every relation a reader would otherwise guess, then repair referent stripping, telegraphese and condition collapse in place
160	4. Confirm one concrete instance survives per non-obvious rule, one caveat survives per action that could go wrong, and the format matches the content under Section 7
161	5. Confirm the body carries nothing from Section 8.1, and that everything removed at this step now sits in the reply. This step is skipped most often, because the process material was correct work and deleting correct work feels wrong. It is not deleted, it moves
162

The reader it asks about is the one who opens the artifact three weeks later with no memory of the conversation that produced it.

---

## 3. CUT RULES

### 3.1 The named rules

- **Question echo.** An opening that restates the prompt before answering it
- **Intent narration.** Announcing the move instead of making it
- **Compliance acknowledgement.** Agreeing to do the work at the top of the work
- **Terminal recap.** A closing paragraph that repeats the body, even accurately
- **Hedge stack.** Two or more uncertainty markers on one claim. Keep the one that is true
- **Importance assertion.** A sentence whose only content is that something matters
- **The conclusion move.** The whole paragraph, not only the phrase that opens it
- **Both-sides padding.** Symmetric pro and con on a question that is not symmetric
- **Empty enumeration.** Naming that there are several things, listing them, analysing none
- **Heading echo.** A first sentence that restates its own heading
- **Restated constraint.** Repeating back a fact the user supplied
- **Effort reporting.** Narrating the work done rather than what it found
- **Count padding.** An item added so a list carries a different number of items. The triad rule counts triads per 150 words and bans none, so leave the count alone and cut something that was never load-bearing

### 3.2 The stated vocabulary

The validator blocks on exactly the terms below, so this list and the gate are one list, and adding a term to either alone is the drift that kept these checks advisory. Section 3.3 of the on-demand rationale records every candidate refused, with the correct writing each would have failed.

Never open a sentence with: "In conclusion", "In summary", "To summarize", "To summarise", "To recap", "To sum up", "It's worth noting", "It is worth noting", "It's important to note", "It is important to note", "Let's explore", "Let's dive in", "Let's take a look", "At the end of the day", "Without further ado", "As we all know", "It goes without saying", "First and foremost", "Last but not least", "With that in mind", "On that note", "That said", "Needless to say", "Simply put", "In essence", "At its core", "In the world of", "When it comes to", "At a high level", "As you can see", "As mentioned above", "As noted above", "As previously noted", "As we have seen", "As discussed above", "In this section", "Put simply", "Generally speaking", "Broadly speaking", "The key takeaway", "The fact of the matter is", "It should be noted", "It must be noted", "By way of background".

Never close a section on: "In summary", "In conclusion", "To summarize", "To summarise", "To recap", "To sum up", "In short", "All in all", "Overall", "Ultimately", "In closing", "To conclude", "To wrap up", "The takeaway", "Net net", "In a nutshell", "Long story short", "To put it simply", "On the whole".

At most one hedge per claim: "might", "may", "could", "perhaps", "maybe", "possibly", "potentially", "probably", "seems", "appears", "arguably", "somewhat", "relatively", "presumably", "likely", "generally", "typically", "I think", "I believe", "tends to", "to some extent", "in some cases", "apparently", "conceivably", "ostensibly", "seemingly", "in theory", "I suspect", "My sense is".

A cross-reference that names its target stays legitimate, so "As noted above" is banned while "the payout window defined under The weekly cycle" is not. A heading followed by a sentence that shares its words and adds no new one is a heading echo: cut the sentence and open on substance.

### 3.4 The two cut rules the validator settles alone

Both resolve without judgement, so the validator blocks on them in a deliverable and reports them as advice on an instruction file.

**Importance assertion.** A sentence of twelve words or fewer carrying one of "important", "critical", "essential", "crucial", "vital", "matters", "significant", "noteworthy" or "fundamental", and carrying no content word of its own beyond that marker and generic filler. A sentence that names what matters and why is left alone.

**Effort reporting.** A sentence opening on "I" or "We" that reaches one of "analysed", "analyzed", "reviewed", "checked", "scored", "scanned", "verified", "examined", "evaluated", "assessed", "investigated" or "audited" within the next few words. A quoted mention is left alone, and so is a sentence whose subject is the process the artifact documents rather than the author. State what the work found, since the work itself is not the deliverable.

---

## 4. KEEP RULES

The anti-robotic half, at the same weight as the cut list. Each item names what a compression pass destroys first.

- **Semantic connectives.** `because`, `so`, `which means`, `unless`, `otherwise`, `since` carry the logic, and deleting one turns an argument into a pile of assertions. The Human Voice cap on `however`, `furthermore`, `moreover`, `additionally` and `consequently` limits rhetoric and never reaches these
- **One concrete instance per non-obvious rule.** The example is what makes a rule applicable
- **The caveat that prevents a wrong action.** A reader who follows the trimmed version and breaks something was not served by the trim
- **The scope qualifier.** `when`, `only when`, `for X but not Y`. A rule stripped of its scope is applied everywhere
- **The noun behind a pronoun.** Name it again once the referent sits more than a clause away
- **The negative case.** "A path string is not verification" is where the reader learns the boundary
- **The specific number.** 33 fixtures, not several fixtures
- **One human beat per roughly 400 words.** An aside, a judgement, a plain admission of what is unknown
- **Grammar.** Articles, copulas and finite verbs are never a compression target, because conciseness removes claims and never syntax

---

## 5. OVER-COMPRESSION SIGNATURES

### 5.1 The five shapes

- **Connective stripping.** Clauses sit next to each other with the relation deleted, so the reader guesses whether the second causes, qualifies or contradicts the first
- **Referent stripping.** Pronouns and bare nouns left with their antecedents cut away
- **Telegraphese.** Dropped articles and copulas, verbless fragments, headline grammar in body text
- **Condition collapse.** A conditional rule flattened into an absolute one, which is a correctness bug rather than a style one
- **Example deletion.** An abstract rule left with nothing showing what it looks like in use

### 5.2 The two the validator counts, and the perimeter they are measured over

Connective stripping and telegraphese leave a numeric trace, so the validator counts them and blocks on a deliverable below either floor. Repair a document that trips one by naming the deleted relations back in and restoring the subject behind every stranded pronoun, never by adding words.

- **Connective floor.** At least 5 semantic connectives per 1000 words of prose
- **Article floor.** At least 30 articles per 1000 words of prose

Both floors are measured over paragraph prose alone, because a ratio only means something where sentences carry the reasoning. Outside the perimeter: frontmatter, a heading at any level, a bullet, a numbered item, a table row, a blockquote, an image, a horizontal rule, a field line such as `**Placement:** Creator deals dashboard`, a hashtag or handle run, a label line whose whole content is one bold or underlined run such as `**Most authentic**`, anything inside a fenced code block, and any HTML comment. Below 200 words of paragraph prose neither floor is applied, since a ratio over fewer words than that is noise.

---

## 7. FORMAT

Prose, bullets and tables are not interchangeable, and picking wrong is how a short answer still reads badly. Three questions decide and the first yes wins: prose where the items differ in weight or their order encodes reasoning, a table where every row shares the same fields, bullets where the items are parallel, independently actionable and three to seven in number. Anything reaching the end without a yes is one paragraph pretending to be a list. Over-bulleting is the main way output turns robotic while looking concise, and the tells are verbless fragments, a bullet that needs the one above it to parse, and a list whose connectives were deleted so the items would line up. Heading density scales with length: under 300 words no headings, above that one per 150 to 400 words.

---

## 8. WHAT A DELIVERABLE NEVER CONTAINS

The reasoning that produced an artifact, the score it earned and the assumptions it rests on are real work, and they belong in the reply beside the export path rather than inside the file the reader opens.

### 8.1 The enumeration

- A scoring section of any kind, whether headed MEQT, HVR, DEAL scoring, Scoring, Self-scan, Hard blockers or Weakest
- A dimension breakdown line, such as `M 4 · E 6 · Q 6 · T 3 · D 3` or its `D · E · A · L` equivalent
- A total, a floor status, a pass or fail verdict, or a score band action
- A hard blocker count or a voice self-scan line, in any wording
- Score commentary, such as a line opening `Weakest:` and naming which dimensions were thin
- An improvement-cycle note, an iteration count or a re-score history
- A bracketed `[Assumes: ...]` tag
- A methodology transcript, a perspective roster, an energy level or a phase-flow trace
- A validation checklist, a gate roster or a template-compliance report
- An attestation footer, a Mode header in visible text, a Template version in visible text, or any other processing metadata

### 8.2 The one sanctioned exception

Line 1 may carry a single HTML comment header, which renders as nothing and is the designed home for the mode, the framework, the score and the template version. A `Stats:` or `Assumes:` line written as an HTML comment directly below sits inside the same exception, for the same reason. Invisible when rendered is the whole test, so a score written as visible text is a violation wherever it sits in the file and a score written as a comment is fine wherever it sits.

### 8.3 Where the reporting goes instead

The reply carries what the artifact does not: the export path with read-back confirmation where the runtime can write files, the score and its verdict at the depth the mode calls for, the voice self-scan line naming the terms fixed and the terms kept with their reason, the assumptions in a form the user can correct before they harden, a short summary and one next step. Producing that report is the point, and moving it out of the artifact does not make it optional.

### 8.4 Two narrow overrides

Where the artifact refines a supplied source, never inject a Mode, Template, Perspectives, Quality Score or Energy header into preserved source structure, since the comment header is for a new artifact and a refinement keeps the source's own opening. Where the packaging renders the deliverable in a panel instead of saving a file, that rendered block is the artifact and the enumeration applies to it unchanged, the report follows the block, and the path is reported as export-equivalent rather than claimed as a save.

---

## 12. THE PRE-EXPORT PASS

Run this after the voice pass and before the export, in order. The first two steps are the cut side and the last three are the keep side, and running only the cut side is the failure this layer exists to prevent.

1. Delete every opener, recap and hedge stack named in Section 3.2, both shapes named in Section 3.4, and the question echo, intent narration, compliance acknowledgement and closing recap the body already carries, including the sentences after the phrase that opened one
2. Apply the reconstruction test to every remaining cut you are tempted to make, and stop at the first one that fails
3. Name every relation a reader would otherwise guess, then repair referent stripping, telegraphese and condition collapse in place
4. Confirm one concrete instance survives per non-obvious rule, one caveat survives per action that could go wrong, and the format matches the content under Section 7
5. Confirm the body carries nothing from Section 8.1, and that everything removed at this step now sits in the reply. This step is skipped most often, because the process material was correct work and deleting correct work feels wrong. It is not deleted, it moves

The machine router for [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md). `SKILL.md` keeps the short routing prose and the

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Primary Detection Signal

```text
$flow | $figjam               -> Flow Mode
FigJam output wording         -> Flow Mode ("make a FigJam flow ...", "a sequence diagram in FigJam")
board notes or a change       -> Flow Mode ("add notes to the FigJam board", "update the FigJam board", any request with a figma.com/board link)
$quick | $q                   -> Quick energy: every row filled from the sources and the defaults with each inferred row marked assumed, sent as the playback, then the gate as usual
another artifact command      -> hand back to the Product Owner packet, whose Interactive Mode asks one question
another artifact's framing    -> hand back to the Product Owner packet, FigJam is then that artifact's subject ("add a task to update the figjam board")
```

```text
a named type the brief does not describe -> compare before intake and ask once, naming the mismatch and the recommended type
```
